title: My puzzle game about building a GPU
author: ikamusume11964
selftext:
Hello everyone, I just shipped a demo for my puzzle game “Hello Triangle: Build a GPU”.

Steam page: [https://store.steampowered.com/app/5395930/](https://store.steampowered.com/app/5395930/).

The game is heavily inspired by Turing Complete. But instead of starting from a NAND gate to build a CPU, in Hello Triangle you start with higher level blocks like Adders and Comparators. By wiring them together, you ultimately build a functional GPU simulator that renders animated 3D scenes pixel-by-pixel. 

The free demo includes Act 1 with 10 levels where you build the circuit to draw a rasterized triangle in the end.

The game was built with a lot of collaboration and automation between claude and codex, lyria and nano banana. 

I would love to hear your thoughts, on whether engineering a GPU through puzzles sounds interesting to you. And if you played the demo, I’d love to know if you feel it is too difficult/easy, and how do you feel about the UX of the circuit building workflow. 

Thanks for checking it out, and let me know what you think!
